To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the time taken to form 50% thromboplastin activity (T50) declines with age and is correlated with FVII level and FVIII activity.
the time taken to form 50% thrombus in plasma in vitro is shorter in older people and that this is associated with lower plasma levels of FVII and FVIII.
the time taken to produce 50% maximal thrombin activity in plasma declines significantly with age.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the coagulation system in normal individuals and in patients with inherited bleeding disorders.
the role of fibrin formation in thrombotic disease and the effect of age upon this process.
the study of the mechanisms of coagulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rate of intrinsic activation is accelerated in plasma from older individuals, possibly due to increased FVII levels.
the time taken for 50% of the maximal thrombin activity to be generated in vitro declines with increasing age of plasma donor.
the rate of thrombin formation is accelerated in older subjects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rate of intrinsic coagulation in plasma is increased with increasing age of plasma donor and this might contribute to the increased incidence of thrombotic disease in older individuals.
there is a negative correlation between age and the rate of thrombin formation in plasma, and that this relationship is partly mediated by the age related increase in plasma FVII levels.
as we age our blood coagulates more quickly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the time taken to form thrombin is shorter in elderly individuals than in young individuals and this might contribute to the increased incidence of thrombotic disease in the elderly.
there is a negative correlation between T-50 (time to reach 50 percent thrombin activity) and age.
the coagulation system accelerates with age and this may have a role in the increased incidence of thrombotic disease in the elderly.
